newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia dismisses Megawati suit against ouster.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia dismisses Megawati suit against ouster.

text.p: An Indonesian court ruled on Thursday it did not have the jurisdiction to hear a lawsuit filed against the government by ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri, dealing a blow to her political hopes.

"The court agrees with all the arguments put forward by the defence that it does not have the authority to hear the case," said I Gde Ketut Sukarata, the head of a three-judge panel of the Central Jakarta State Court.
Megawati's supporters in the packed courtroom cheered when her chief lawyer, R.O. Tambunan, said he would appeal.
Hundreds of riot police and troops, backed by guard dogs, an armoured car with a water cannon and a fire engine, stood by at the court complex to prevent any violence.
However witnesses said there were no visible signs of tension. Police dispersed a crowd of about 200 people waiting outside the court.

Megawati, daughter of Indonesias's late founding president Sukarno, had sued the government and the military over her June dismissal from the leadership of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) at a government-backed congress called by a rival party faction.

Government defence lawyers argued that the case was an internal party matter and the court had no jurisdiction. Lawyers for the military, meanwhile, said it had provided security for the congress, held in the Sumatran city of Medan, under its constitutional duty to guard large gatherings.

Megawati became the focal point of a rare burst of dissent against the government after her ouster and hundreds of people gathered almost daily at the PDI headquarters in Jakarta in the days after the congress to vent their criticism.

Riots erupted in the city on July 27 after police raided the headquarters to evict Megawati's supporters. Five people died and scores of buildings and vehicles were set ablaze in the violence, the worst in Jakarta for over two decades.
Megawati has also filed a lawsuit against the government and the country's national election body for rejecting her list of candidates for next year's parliamentary elections.
She is also suing the mayor of East Jakarta for closing down her new headquarters on the ground that it violated residential zoning restrictions.
The Christian-Nationalist PDI, the ruling Golkar and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) are the only groups legally permitted to contest elections.
The government recognises only the faction that ousted Megawati as representing the PDI.
Political analysts have said the government moved to sideline Megawati because it feared she could draw votes away from Golkar in the elections.
